name: Feedyio
summary: Shopify product-feed engine (by happyapps.cz) that generates and syncs feeds for Google, Meta, Pinterest, TikTok, Bing and 130-plus marketplaces and price-comparison sites, with strong coverage of the Central European channels (Heureka, Glami, Kaufland, Favi). Custom XML, CSV, TXT or JSON feeds are built from your own Liquid template, with category mapping, attribute rules and validation before products get rejected. Launched May 2022.
best_for: Shopify merchants who need several feeds at once, in formats they control (custom XML, CSV, TXT or JSON built from their own template) and especially those selling into Central and Eastern European marketplaces and price-comparison sites, with a catalogue that fits inside a published tier
skip_if: you need one Google Shopping feed and nothing else, where the older and far more widely reviewed feed apps cover the same ground; or your catalogue runs past 65,000 products, which is where the published ladder ends
honest_knock: Two gates decide your bill and neither is about how much value the feeds create. The first is catalogue size: the ladder counts products and variants, and it runs further than the Shopify listing suggests: the listing stops at Pro ($29.99, 6,000 products) and says additional plans are available, while the vendor's own pricing page publishes five more tiers up to $119.99 for 65,000 products. The second is freshness: the free tier updates products once a day and hourly updates start at $9.99, which matters when stock moves faster than a day. Multi-market and multi-language feeds only appear at $19.99. The app is also younger and smaller than the shelf leaders: launched 16 May 2022 by happyapps.cz in Prague, with 115 reviews against thousands for the established Google Shopping feed apps. And the standout integrations: Heureka, Zboží.cz, Árukereső, Glami, Favi, Kaufland: are Central and Eastern European channels; that is the app's real edge, but it is not an edge if you only sell through Google and Meta.

pricing.notes: (read 2026-09-10 on apps.shopify.com/product-feed-10 and feedyio.com/pricing) Nine published tiers, billed in USD every 30 days through Shopify. The Shopify listing shows only the first four. Free is permanent and covers up to 30 products or 100 variants, one feed, the primary market only, a daily product update and email support. Basic at $9.99 a month raises that to 1,000 products or 2,000 variants, up to five feeds, hourly product updates and the named comparison-shopping integrations (Heureka, Favi and similar), still on the primary market and language only. Advanced at $19.99 covers 2,500 products or 5,000 variants, up to ten feeds, and all markets and languages. Pro at $29.99 covers 6,000 products or 12,000 variants and up to 30 feeds. The listing stops there and says additional plans are available; the vendor's own pricing page prices them: Enterprise $39.99 (10,000 products / 20,000 variants / 40 feeds), Enterprise Plus $59.99 (20,000 / 40,000 / 40), Enterprise Plus 2 $89.99 (30,000 / 60,000 / 40), Enterprise Plus 3 $99.99 (50,000 / 100,000 / 40) and Enterprise Plus 4 $119.99 (65,000 / 130,000 / 40). Every paid tier has a 7-day free trial. One inconsistency on that page: the line under the table says every paid plan includes Shopify markets, translations and inventory levels, while the Basic card above it lists the primary market and primary language only — the Shopify listing agrees with the card, so confirm before buying Basic for a second market.

price_history.method: Stable = every amount on the vendor's pricing page identical across >= 3 of our reads over >= 30 days. A change is listed only after we confirmed the new price on the page, with a verbatim quote. Differences in raw readings are never published on their own.

compare_with.name: Simprosys Google Shopping Feed, Koongo: Sell on Marketplaces
compare_with.why: the difference is breadth of channel against depth of track record. Simprosys is the shelf leader for the Google, Microsoft, Meta and Pinterest set and carries thousands of reviews (read 10 September 2026 on the Shopify App Store); Feedyio carries 115 and is three years old. What Feedyio has instead is the template editor (you write your own XML, CSV, TXT or JSON in Liquid rather than picking from a fixed list) and a preconfigured set of European comparison and marketplace channels that the Google-first apps treat as an afterthought. If your channels are Google and Meta, buy on track record. If your channels include Heureka, Glami, Kaufland or a marketplace that wants a feed shaped its own way, Feedyio is the one built for that, and the free tier lets you check the output shape before paying.

purchase.disclosure: Where purchase.affiliate is true, purchase.handoff_url is our own review page for the product; the vendor button on that page is a marked affiliate link and AIBuilder Marketplace may earn a commission at no extra cost to the buyer. Commission never changes what a record says, and products are not ranked by commission. Where it is false the link is the vendor's plain site. claims.observed: The Free plan says Up to 100 products and up to 300 variants, one feed, the primary market and the primary language only; the Billing usage shows 14 imported products and 23 variants with 0 remaining.
claims.plan: Free plan; Basic approval screen viewed, not approved
claims.comparability: Free plan card versus the usage bars on the Billing page of one development store.
claims.buying_consequence: The free plan is limited to 100 products, 300 variants and one feed, in one market and one language.

claims.observed: The Billing page counts 14 imported products and 23 variants, while the Heureka feed card counts 12 products and 18 variants. The difference was not explained.
claims.plan: Free plan; Basic approval screen viewed, not approved
claims.comparability: Billing usage versus the product count on the feed card on one development store.
claims.buying_consequence: The product counts of the plan and of the feed differ, so check what the feed really contains.

claims.observed: A Heureka feed was Live about 3 minutes after the install click, with 3 clicks for the feed itself, 12 products and 18 variants, and an XML preview with the Heureka SHOPITEM fields.
claims.plan: Free plan; Basic approval screen viewed, not approved
claims.comparability: Feed card and XML preview versus the store catalog; the feed was never opened by a service.
claims.buying_consequence: A Heureka feed can be built within minutes on the Free plan; Heureka itself did not load it.

claims.observed: The feed shows 5 unlisted items and 36 warnings. The causes are products out of stock, products not published in the Online Store or a store that is password protected, and a missing standardized product type.
claims.plan: Free plan; Basic approval screen viewed, not approved
claims.comparability: Feed issues dialog versus the test products of one development store.
claims.buying_consequence: The feed leaves out products that are out of stock or not published and warns about missing product types, so fix the catalog first.

claims.claim: Last opened by a service: No opens recorded
claims.observed: The feed card says that no service has opened the feed; it was not submitted to Heureka or Glami.
claims.plan: Free plan; Basic approval screen viewed, not approved
claims.comparability: Feed card status versus a feed that was never submitted to a shopping channel.
claims.buying_consequence: The test says nothing about whether Heureka or Glami accept the feed.

claims.observed: The Basic plan lists integrations with heureka, zbozi, favi and biano, up to 5 feeds, markets, translations and an hourly products update; none of these was tried because Basic could not be approved.
claims.plan: Free plan; Basic approval screen viewed, not approved
claims.comparability: Plan card feature list versus a test limited to the Free plan.
claims.buying_consequence: The extra Basic features were not tested.

claims.observed: The plan cards and the Shopify approval screen for Basic both show a 7-day free trial, ending on 24 Nov., with $9,99 due 24 Nov. The sentence about a test charge was not on the screen, a payment method was asked and Approve was greyed out, so it was not approved.
claims.plan: Free plan; Basic approval screen viewed, not approved
claims.comparability: Plan card wording versus the Shopify approval screen; nothing was approved.
claims.buying_consequence: Basic starts with a 7-day trial, but a payment method is needed even on a development store.

claims.observed: On the Free plan Cancel subscription is greyed out, so there is nothing to cancel. Removing the app goes through Settings, Apps, Uninstall, where the dialog says the app data will be deleted, a request goes to the developer within 48 hours to delete personal customer information, and a reason is needed before Uninstall is active.
claims.plan: Free plan; Basic approval screen viewed, not approved
claims.comparability: Billing page and uninstall dialog on a development store with only the Free plan.
claims.buying_consequence: There is no paid plan to cancel on Free; the only way out of the app is to uninstall it, with a reason.

claims.observed: The plan card says Basic $9.99 a month and the Shopify approval screen says $9,99 USD every 30 days, a total of $9,99 due 24 Nov. plus any applicable taxes. It was not approved and nothing was billed.
claims.plan: Free plan; Basic approval screen viewed, not approved
claims.comparability: Plan card price versus the approval screen amount; no stored cost rule was compared.
claims.buying_consequence: The price of $9.99 a month matches between the plan card and the approval screen, before taxes.

exit_test.what: The app was installed on our Shopify development store, which we set up, and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser. On 17 November 2026 the session tested Feedyio on a Shopify development store: the install, a Heureka feed with its XML preview and issue list, the Free plan and the plan cards, the Shopify approval screen for Basic (not approved) and the uninstall dialog, after which the app was uninstalled. Nothing was paid and the feed was not loaded in Heureka. Install: the App Store listing (English) is the product feed app Feedyio, from happyapps.cz. Install was started at about 12:02:46; the first click only showed the apps list, the Install app dialog (View customer data, View staff and contributor data, View and edit store data) came at the second click and the app (version 3.6.0) opened at about 12:04. The start screen showed the banner We are indexing your products and the usage Plan usage: 0 of 1 feeds, 0 of 100 products, 0 of 300 variants. A promo popup for another product of the vendor had to be closed. There was no plan screen and no Shopify approval screen at install. Core action: Create feed, search Heureka, Select (the market heureka.cz). The app said Saved and regenerated. About 3 minutes after the install click, with 3 clicks for the feed itself, the feed was Live, last sync at 12:04. The feed card says Heureka Live, Heureka, US, en, shows a feed link, Products 12, Variants / items 18, Unlisted / warnings 5 / 36 and Last opened by a service: No opens recorded. Feed preview shows XML with SHOP and SHOPITEM and the fields ITEM_ID, PRODUCTNAME, URL, IMGURL, PRICE_VAT, MANUFACTURER, PRODUCTNO, CONDITION, DESCRIPTION, ITEMGROUP_ID and DELIVERY_DATE; for The Inventory Not Tracked Snowboard the PRICE_VAT is 949.95. Feed issues (click on 5 / 36): unlisted Product excluded: Out of stock; critical Product not published in Online Store or Store is Protected (your product is not published to the online store or your store is password protected); critical Standardized product type missing. Not done: loading the feed in Heureka itself, Glami, a second market. No one has opened the feed, so we do not know if Heureka accepts it. Plans: the Billing page shows Current plan Free ($0): All time free, Up to 100 products, Up to 300 variants, Only primary Shopify market, Only primary language, Create 1 Feed. The usage there says Imported 14 products and 23 variants with 0 remaining, while the feed itself counts 12 products and 18 variants; we did not find out why. Cancel subscription is greyed out on Free. Basic $9.99 a month has 7 days free trial, Up to 1 000 products, Up to 2 000 variants, Product Metafields and Metaobjects, Shop Metafields, Ability to use Shopify markets, translations and inventory levels, Hourly products update, Integrations (heureka, zbozi, favi, biano) and Create up to 5 Feeds. Advanced $19.99 has 2 500 products, 5 000 variants and up to 10 feeds. Pro $29.99 (6 000 and 12 000), Enterprise $39.99 (10 000 and 20 000) and Enterprise Plus $59.99 (20 000 and 40 000) are billed monthly with 7 days free trial; we did not scroll further. Checkout: Select Basic opened the Shopify Approve subscription screen, plan Basic 2, $9,99 USD every 30 days, You have a 7-day free trial ending on 24 Nov., a subtotal and total of $9,99 due 24 Nov, and an Add payment method row. The sentence about a test charge was NOT on this screen, the Approve button was greyed out and a payment method was asked, so we did not approve; Cancel was pressed and nothing was charged. Basic cannot be tried on this development store without a payment method. Cancelling: on Free there is nothing to cancel because Cancel subscription is greyed out. Removing the app goes through Settings, Apps, Uninstall; the dialog Uninstall Feedyio? says you will no longer be able to use the app, that data managed by the app, such as discounts, will be deleted, and that a request goes to the developer within 48 hours to delete personal customer information. The Uninstall button is active only after a reason is chosen (Testing multiple apps). Not tested: whether Heureka or Glami load the feed, a second market or language, Basic or Advanced after adding a payment method, the integrations (Heureka trusted badge, review consent), Import orders, Translations, the fetch schedule and channel rejections. Clean up: the app was uninstalled after the test and no longer shows in the list of installed apps; the feed went with it. Plan Basic was not approved and no theme change was saved. Our own tabs were closed. The apps list with an account name was not kept as evidence. No kit records were entered.
exit_test.awkward: The billing page counts 14 products and 23 variants while the feed counts 12 and 18, five feed warnings come from products that are out of stock, not published or without a standardized product type, and Basic needs a payment method even on a development store.

friction.export_route: No export or reimport was performed; no file was downloaded or examined. The two categorised kit records were not entered; the objects tested were not kit records.

not_tested: Original store creation and identity check, which we did ourselves.
Loading the feed in Heureka or Glami, so it is unknown if they accept it.
A second market or language in a feed.
Basic or Advanced, because the approval screen asked for a payment method.
The integrations, Import orders, Translations and the fetch schedule.
Support, export and reimport.

exit_test.what: The app was installed on our Shopify development store, which we set up, and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser. On 17 November 2026 the session tested Feedyio on a Shopify development store: the install, a Heureka feed with its XML preview and issue list, the Free plan and the plan cards, the Shopify approval screen for Basic (not approved) and the uninstall dialog, after which the app was uninstalled. Nothing was paid and the feed was not loaded in Heureka. Install: the App Store listing (English) is the product feed app Feedyio, from happyapps.cz. Install was started at about 12:02:46; the first click only showed the apps list, the Install app dialog (View customer data, View staff and contributor data, View and edit store data) came at the second click and the app (version 3.6.0) opened at about 12:04. The start screen showed the banner We are indexing your products and the usage Plan usage: 0 of 1 feeds, 0 of 100 products, 0 of 300 variants. A promo popup for another product of the vendor had to be closed. There was no plan screen and no Shopify approval screen at install. Core action: Create feed, search Heureka, Select (the market heureka.cz). The app said Saved and regenerated. About 3 minutes after the install click, with 3 clicks for the feed itself, the feed was Live, last sync at 12:04. The feed card says Heureka Live, Heureka, US, en, shows a feed link, Products 12, Variants / items 18, Unlisted / warnings 5 / 36 and Last opened by a service: No opens recorded. Feed preview shows XML with SHOP and SHOPITEM and the fields ITEM_ID, PRODUCTNAME, URL, IMGURL, PRICE_VAT, MANUFACTURER, PRODUCTNO, CONDITION, DESCRIPTION, ITEMGROUP_ID and DELIVERY_DATE; for The Inventory Not Tracked Snowboard the PRICE_VAT is 949.95. Feed issues (click on 5 / 36): unlisted Product excluded: Out of stock; critical Product not published in Online Store or Store is Protected (your product is not published to the online store or your store is password protected); critical Standardized product type missing. Not done: loading the feed in Heureka itself, Glami, a second market. No one has opened the feed, so we do not know if Heureka accepts it. Plans: the Billing page shows Current plan Free ($0): All time free, Up to 100 products, Up to 300 variants, Only primary Shopify market, Only primary language, Create 1 Feed. The usage there says Imported 14 products and 23 variants with 0 remaining, while the feed itself counts 12 products and 18 variants; we did not find out why. Cancel subscription is greyed out on Free. Basic $9.99 a month has 7 days free trial, Up to 1 000 products, Up to 2 000 variants, Product Metafields and Metaobjects, Shop Metafields, Ability to use Shopify markets, translations and inventory levels, Hourly products update, Integrations (heureka, zbozi, favi, biano) and Create up to 5 Feeds. Advanced $19.99 has 2 500 products, 5 000 variants and up to 10 feeds. Pro $29.99 (6 000 and 12 000), Enterprise $39.99 (10 000 and 20 000) and Enterprise Plus $59.99 (20 000 and 40 000) are billed monthly with 7 days free trial; we did not scroll further. Checkout: Select Basic opened the Shopify Approve subscription screen, plan Basic 2, $9,99 USD every 30 days, You have a 7-day free trial ending on 24 Nov., a subtotal and total of $9,99 due 24 Nov, and an Add payment method row. The sentence about a test charge was NOT on this screen, the Approve button was greyed out and a payment method was asked, so we did not approve; Cancel was pressed and nothing was charged. Basic cannot be tried on this development store without a payment method. Cancelling: on Free there is nothing to cancel because Cancel subscription is greyed out. Removing the app goes through Settings, Apps, Uninstall; the dialog Uninstall Feedyio? says you will no longer be able to use the app, that data managed by the app, such as discounts, will be deleted, and that a request goes to the developer within 48 hours to delete personal customer information. The Uninstall button is active only after a reason is chosen (Testing multiple apps). Not tested: whether Heureka or Glami load the feed, a second market or language, Basic or Advanced after adding a payment method, the integrations (Heureka trusted badge, review consent), Import orders, Translations, the fetch schedule and channel rejections. Clean up: the app was uninstalled after the test and no longer shows in the list of installed apps; the feed went with it. Plan Basic was not approved and no theme change was saved. Our own tabs were closed. The apps list with an account name was not kept as evidence. No kit records were entered.
exit_test.awkward: The billing page counts 14 products and 23 variants while the feed counts 12 and 18, five feed warnings come from products that are out of stock, not published or without a standardized product type, and Basic needs a payment method even on a development store.
